raw_response:
I am thinking about this year same as last year. Change too much, you lose money. I do what works.

I have 9 mu. Five mu I keep in cotton — my family always grew cotton, and I know it. The other 4 mu I do wheat in winter, then maize after the wheat comes off in summer. That way the land is never empty and I get two harvests from the same ground.

For cotton, the dealer sells me Bt seed — the one that the bollworm does not eat so bad. My neighbor Old Wang, he grew this one, got good bolls, so I use the same. Before planting I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu (the 15-15-15 kind, 50 jin each bag, so about 50 kg), and when the cotton is flowering I top with 1 bag of urea, maybe 20 kg. Cotton eats a lot, if I give too little the bolls stay small. Better give a little extra than watch the bolls drop. Pesticide — cotton needs spraying many times, aphid, red spider, bollworm even with Bt. I spray maybe 7 or 8 times, whenever I see bugs. Water from the well 3 times — after planting, at flower, and when bolls are filling.

For wheat, I plant the improved seed from the town cooperative, same one everyone around here uses. Before sowing I plow with the rotary machine (I pay the tractor man 40 yuan per mu) and spread 1.5 bags compound fertilizer. In spring when the wheat turns green I top with 1 bag urea. I water 3 times — spring green, jointing, and when the grain is filling. Only spray once or twice for aphid if I see them bad.

For maize after wheat, hybrid seed — the short-season one so it ripens before cold. I put a little compound fertilizer in the hole at planting, then top with urea when it is knee-high. Maize grows fast, no time for mistakes. Water 2 times if rain is short. Spray once for the borer.

My family has 6 people, some go work in the factory, so I do most of the field work myself with my wife. I hire help only for cotton picking. Every yuan on fertilizer counts, but I have seen what happens when you save too much — the harvest is small and then you save nothing.
